Open Mind, an open research group

Find the best theory of consciousness by 2027

An open-source effort, run in public. All our code and data are free.

ContributeRead the findings

01The question

Nobody knows which brain activity makes an experience

You are having experiences right now: sights, sounds, thoughts. Each comes from activity in your brain, but nobody can say which activity.

There are dozens of theories. In 2025 the largest head-to-head test so far pitted two of them against each other. Neither won.

So we cannot yet tell whether a patient who cannot respond is aware, or what an anaesthetic switches off.

What scientists agree on

02Where we are

We can tell awake from deep sleep, but no theory has passed a fair test

Track the progress

03Found so far

What we have found so far

  • Our first theory failed. We sealed a test of it in advance and ran it on 237 awakenings from 35 sleepers. All four measures came out flat.
  • A popular brain measure adds little. Signal complexity is often used as a sign of consciousness. About 97% of its power to tell waking from deep sleep comes from the recording's simple mix of slow and fast waves.
  • Dreams can be tested on open data, injured patients cannot. About 2,400 open awakenings come with a report of experience. No open recordings exist from brain-injured patients.

All 10 findings and closed routes, with their evidence

04How we work

How we test a theory

We write each test down and fingerprint it before we open the data. A result counts only if it holds on people the method never saw, and survives someone trying to break it.

Our approach and what counts as done

05Open data

Every consciousness dataset, free in one place

We checked every open dataset for one thing: do we know whether the person was experiencing anything?

We list 134 datasets, where each lives and under which terms. Today, reports of experience are open only for sleep.
